title: SIM-032 active-tether follow-cam — controls / estimation science (autonomy: detection, estimation, reel & flyer control, launch / retrieve / dock, abnormal events)
evidence: Numerical, uncalibrated simulation only (point-mass tethered flyer, quasi-static straight line with sag correction, synthetic activity kinematics). NOT physical verification: M-070 not_run, G-MATURE closed. No purchasing, outreach or physical tests. Numbers marked ASSUMED are placeholders.

scripts.lib/traces.mjs: back-pack motion traces: ski runs from simulateRun/FULLRUN_PLAN, synthetic queue/chairlift/surface lift/walk/gondola/cat-track/bus/sit-down
scripts.lib/detect.mjs: ride start/stop/fall detector (IMU + GNSS + baro, post-lift lockout) and scoring

hypotheses.claim: A back-worn IMU (+GNSS +baro) detects ride starts in <1.0 s (p90) with <1 false launch per ski day and no missed starts; chairlift, queue, walking, gondola never trigger.
hypotheses.method: Detector on synthetic sensor streams (ICM-42688 + AHRS budget, MAX-M10S 10 Hz with 5 % outages, BMP390 with in-pack dynamic-pressure error). 60 project skier runs (4 style presets × 12 seeds + 12 falls), 12 slow "glide-away" starts, 40 simulated days (15 laps queue+chair/surface lift, walks, gondola, cat tracks, sit-downs; 105 h non-ski motion), bus descent separately. Start latency measured from push-off.

full.stopLatencyNote: p50 0.38–0.52 s for carving/short turns (decel trigger); moguls (24°, 4.5 m/s) 2.2 s because the hockey-stop decel minus gravity stays below the 2.5 m/s² trigger and the speed rule fires instead

hypotheses.verdict: SUPPORTED IN SIMULATION, with conditions. p90 0.98 s from push-off, 0 missed, 0 false launches in 40 synthetic days (95 % upper bound ≈0.075/day) — but only with GNSS (speed gate 2.8 m/s > fixed-grip chair speed), a descent gate, ski-vibration gate, a from-rest condition and a post-lift lockout (30 m of non-ascending travel). Removing the lockout gives ≈2 false launches/day on chairlift unload ramps; IMU-only without baro gives ≈4/day and misses starts. Gentle glide-away starts take 3.4–4.7 s. Every bus/car descent produced a false start → the product needs a ski-session arm (dock latch + "armed" state set by the first lift ride or a pole-tap gesture) or a resort geofence. Activity models are synthetic: a labelled field log (≥50 ski days, several resorts) is required before any claim.

hypotheses.claim: Tension + 2-axis line angle (+ reel encoder, pack GNSS/IMU) alone suffice to estimate the apparent wind at the flyer to ±1 m/s, plus flyer position and lift margin, without any flyer air data.
hypotheses.method: Shadow-mode estimators on identical (oracle-flown) trajectories over the 48-case ensemble. Tether-only estimator = exit-angle sag correction + line kinematics + a 3-state EKF on the wind vector inverting the aero model (AoA referenced to the line), gated by an attached-flow prior. Variants: realistic sensors, calibrated load cell & polar, + flyer IMU specific force, perfect sensors (structural floor), and flyer air data (pitot + vane + attitude). Plus a steady-flight test (12 m line, carving, calm) with a one-factor-at-a-time error budget (dbg_eq.mjs).
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED. Structural reason: the aerodynamic force on a tethered wing is almost parallel to the line, so the rotation of the apparent wind about the tether axis is (nearly) unobservable from tension + line angle; only the skier's turns make it observable over time, and any force-scale error (load-cell scale 5 %, polar 8 %) is dumped into that weak direction (steady test: mean wind error 0.7 → 2.2–3.3 m/s from a single factor). Even with perfect sensors the 48-case ensemble gives |va| error p50 ≈5.6 m/s (quasi-static assumption and model mismatch during the large swings the controller does not suppress); in steady flight the floor is ≈1.3–1.5 m/s p50 with heavy tails. Flyer position from the exit angle is ≈1.0–1.6 m p50 (≈7–10 % of line length; pack yaw and sag dominate). Low-lift (LM<1.3) detection recall ≤0.2. With a flyer pitot + AoA vane + attitude the horizontal wind error is 1.358 m/s p50 / 5.444 m/s p95 — still not ±1 m/s p95. Tension remains a good fast *tension* signal for the reel loop, not an anemometer.

hypotheses.claim: A single tension (reel) loop can replace a flight controller on the glider (and kite).
hypotheses.method: exp3 closed loop over 48 cases: A1 = reel admittance only, flyer with fixed bridle pitch + spoilers and an open-loop launch pitch schedule; A2 = + roll loop; A3 = + AoA/pitch-vs-line loop and spoiler elevation loop; with launch from the back and started in flight at 12 m (launch excluded). Steady equilibrium tests (dbg_eq) on straight and carving runs.
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED for the glider; not supported for the kite. Physics found in the model: (1) lift on a tethered wing points along the line, so lateral position is neutral/unstable — a wing with no roll feedback drifts to the window edge where its line-referenced AoA collapses (A1 diverged laterally in ~3 s even in straight, steady running; with a roll loop of bank > lateral angle, K_φ≈1.8, it held); (2) on a 15° slope the wind window tilts forward with the slope and the weight component along the slope pulls the flyer forward → overflight and slack unless drag (spoilers) holds it back; (3) a high-L/D wing at window elevations <40° is in a deep power zone (AoA 40–90°) from which only a ≈80° pitch (flag-out) range recovers. A1 glider: 0.14 availability, flyer median height 0.05 m (on/near the snow). The kite A1 kept flying more (avail 0.469) but with median peak body force 310.623 N (power-zone dragging). Minimum flyer control set: roll (steering), line-referenced pitch with flag-out range, spoilers/depower, and AoA/airspeed sensing.

hypotheses.claim: "Fly it like a kite" (pay out with surplus tension, reel in when tension/lift drops) keeps the flyer airborne through lulls and tail winds and gives ≥80 % filming availability.
hypotheses.method: exp3 A3 variants (admittance reel law, flyer force target 2×T_set so the surplus is paid out, length target 15 m glider / 12 m kite; launch gate: est. apparent wind ≥1.3 V_stall and skier accel <2 m/s² for 0.3 s).
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED as implemented. Best availability (share of riding time with line >5 m and flyer >2 m above the pack) is 0.503 (kite, oracle — labelled sensitivity) and 0.459 (glider already at 12 m); with launch from the back and real estimates 0.072 (glider) / 0.412 (kite). Every variant has snow contacts in every run. Tail winds remain the hard case (glider-in-flight 0.367). Reel-in does supply airspeed (reel-in peaks ≈5.5–7 m/s used) but cannot make up for apparent wind near zero for more than L/v_r ≈2–3 s. The law itself is sound for the reel (smooth, ≤8 m/s² command slew), but the reel cannot stabilise the flyer: that needs H3's flyer loops working at short line lengths, which they did not.

hypotheses.claim: An 80 g drone outrunner (MN3508 KV380 class, direct drive, 4S, Ø25 mm drum) gives enough reel bandwidth, speed (≥6 m/s in) and pull (≥25 N) with <150 W peak and <0.2 Wh per run.
hypotheses.method: Reel truth model: drum + rotor inertia (reflected ≈0.27 kg at the line), viscous + Coulomb friction, V/I-limited torque–speed envelope, FOC current loop, 500 Hz velocity loop with tension feed-forward from a 22 ms-delayed load cell. Variants M0 (2207 KV900 + 5:1, 3S), M1, M2 (6S, Ø32 mm).
hypotheses.verdict: PARTLY SUPPORTED. M1 reached ≈5.5–7 m/s reel-in and kept energy at ≈0.06–0.16 Wh per 100 s run (≈2–6 Wh per day of 35 runs — small next to the camera), but peak electrical power p90 is 160.903 W (spikes when braking/accelerating against snatch loads) → size the ESC/battery for ≈250 W bursts. M0 (geared, 3S) is too slow (reel-in max -2.611 m/s) and drew higher peaks; M2 (6S, larger drum) gave the fastest reel-in at slightly lower peak power. Reflected reel inertia (0.27 kg > flyer mass) means tension spikes are set by the series shock spring (150 N/m used) — the spring, not the motor bandwidth, is what keeps snatch loads bounded; without it the stiff line produced 40–55 N snatches at launch.

hypotheses.claim: Automatic launch from the back succeeds on ≥95 % of detected rides within 5 s, with no snow contact.
hypotheses.method: exp3 full runs (launch from a dock 0.27 m above the pack, high-lift climb-out, ≤2 m/s pay-out while the line is short) vs. "in-flight" variants started at 12 m.
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED. The short-line phase (<5 m) is the crux: a carving skier moves the pack laterally ±≈4 m at 0.35 Hz with ≈1.2 g, the flyer at 1–5 m is whipped through the window, stalls, hits the snow (which rises behind the skier on a slope) and is dragged. Launches succeeded reliably only when the skier ran straight (dbg_eq straight test: 3 m in ≈1.5 s, 15 m in ≈7 s) or when the flyer was already at ≥6 m (stable in carving in the steady test). Recommendation: launch only on a straight glide (push-off phase or a traverse; gate on low lateral acceleration for ≥1 s), pay out ≤2 m/s until 6 m, and abort to dock on the first stall. Launch-gate refusal adds ≈11.989 s of riding without footage per run.

hypotheses.claim: On a detected stop the system retrieves and docks the flyer on the back within 10 s with ≤1.5 m/s relative speed.
hypotheses.method: exp3: retrieve at 5 m/s (1.5 m/s below 3 m, 0.6 m/s below 1 m), flyer depowered to a 6 N retrieval tension with spoilers; dock = within 0.25 m of the cradle. Variant "predock": user gesture 6 s before the planned stop → retrieve while still riding.
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED for the glider, borderline for the kite. Retrieval time is fine (p90 3.5–15 s), but the glider arrives at the cradle at 5.1 m/s p50 (≈2 J relative KE, ≥1.5 m/s in most docks): after the skier stops there is no apparent wind, the only airspeed is the reel speed, and a 12 N/m² wing cannot fly slower than ≈4.6 m/s. Docking while still riding (predock) lowers it to 3.36 m/s p50. The low-wing-loading kite docks at 1.57 m/s p50 (0.421 of docks <1.5 m/s). Conclusion: a back dock needs a light, low-wing-loading flyer and a compliant capture funnel; for a glider, land beside the skier instead.

hypotheses.claim: On a skier fall, holding the line and letting the flyer land (flag-out) is safer than reeling it in to the back.
hypotheses.method: exp4: falls at 18/27 s into a ride (6 wind cases × 2), flyer at 12 m, fall detected by the IMU detector (p90 0.62 s); abort=reel vs abort=hold, glider and kite.
hypotheses.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED — neither policy is safe in the model. The fallen skier keeps sliding; the line drags the flyer down toward the body in both policies (flyer within 0.5 m of the helmet at >3 m/s relative speed in 0.833 (glider) and 0.25–0.333 (kite) of falls; line tension after the fall p90 ≈48–55 N on a person who is down). Reel-in reaches a safe state faster (glider p50 3.92 s vs 10.5 s). Needed: a tension-limited breakaway/weak link at the pack (release ≈15–20 N, ASSUMED), line cutter, and a flyer that is harmless on contact (KE and soft structure), not a smarter abort law.

hypotheses.claim: The flyer is always stowed before the skier reaches the chair-loading point.
hypotheses.method: exp4 gentle lift approach (snow-plough 0.8–2 m/s², no hockey stop) → stop detection when ≤1.5 m/s; stowed time = detection + retrieve/dock time from exp3.
hypotheses.verdict: SUPPORTED ON TIME, NOT ON SAFETY. Stowed ≈3.83 s (glider) / 9.6 s (kite) p90 after slowing to 1.5 m/s, inside an ASSUMED 10–20 s corral budget — but those docks are the fast, uncontrolled ones of H7, among other people in the lift queue. Required interlocks: OSM aerialway geofence (bottom stations, retrieve when <80 m and decelerating), dock-latch sensor, haptic/acoustic alarm if not latched when ascent is detected, and no launch until the post-lift lockout clears.

hypotheses.claim: Because the window zenith tilts forward with the slope, the line rises steeply from the pack and the clothesline hazard to crossing skiers disappears beyond ≈2 m.
hypotheses.method: exp3 line profile (chord + sag) during riding: share of time the line or flyer is <1.9 m above snow at 1–8 m horizontal distance; exp4 share of airborne time with the flyer itself at head height 1.5–15 m from the skier.
hypotheses.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED in closed loop. The geometry argument holds in steady flight (equilibrium at 60–70° window elevation ⇒ line >1.9 m beyond ≈1 m), but the simulated flights spend much time low: the flyer itself is at head height 1.5–15 m from the skier for 0.28 (glider) / 0.212 (kite) of airborne time, and the line or flyer is below 1.9 m at 3 m behind the skier for 0.6 (glider) / 0.505 (kite) of airborne riding time (median run), and the line passes within ≈0.01–0.08 m (p10 over runs) of the helmet centre (headClear ≥1.0 m fails). Third-party safety therefore depends entirely on solving H6 (short-line phase) and H11.

hypotheses.claim: The flyer's kinetic energy stays below 14.9 J (FAA Cat 2 line used by the project).
hypotheses.method: exp3 KE (ground frame beyond 1.5 m from the rider, rider frame within).
hypotheses.verdict: FALSIFIED. A tethered flyer moves with the skier, so its ground-frame KE has a floor of ½·m·v_skier² (glider 150 g: 13.7 J at 13.5 m/s); the swings and crosswind dives of a tethered wing roughly double its speed (median peak KE 32.433 J even for the 100 g kite with oracle states). To hold 14.9 J with 2× swing speed the flyer must weigh ≈40 g — or the 14.9 J rule must be argued in the rider frame (it cannot when the flyer is >1.5 m away).

physicsFindings: Line-referenced AoA: AoA = pitch-vs-line − asin(u·n). A bridled/tow-hooked wing at window elevation ε sits at AoA ≈ aB + (90° − ε): falling 20° lower in the window adds 20° of AoA → stall/power zone. Elevation control = drag (spoilers/depower) at fixed AoA.

High-L/D (≈11) glider: natural equilibrium ε ≈ 85–88° (near the zenith) where weight and small drag make it overfly and go slack; flying at 60–70° needs L/D_eff ≈2 (spoilers out) — i.e. the glider is flown as a draggy kite.

On a slope the apparent wind is parallel to the slope, so the window zenith tilts forward by the slope angle and gravity has an along-wind component (W·sin θ) that pushes the flyer toward overflight; the snow surface rises behind the skier, so a flyer that falls back in the window hits the snow (uphill).
Lift points along the line ⇒ lateral position is neutrally stable at best; roll steering with bank > lateral angle (K_φ≈1.8) plus rate damping scaled by m·L/Lift is required.
The window must be defined on the mean course (τ≈2.5 s), not the instantaneous skier velocity, which swings ±45° every 1.45 s.
Short line (<5 m) + carving ⇒ the pack's ±4 m lateral oscillation whips the flyer; ≥6 m the line low-passes it (stable in the steady carving test at 6 and 12 m).
Snatch loads: slack→taut with a Dyneema line produced 40–55 N; a 150 N/m series shock spring at the fairlead bounds them — required for body force ≤40 N.
Estimator observability: aero force ∥ line ⇒ rotation of va about the line is unobservable instantaneously; turns provide observability; force-scale errors map into wind direction errors.

recommendedArchitecture.summary: Do not pursue "tension-only" autonomy. If the active-tether direction continues, it needs: a light (≤60–100 g), low-wing-loading kite-like flyer with roll steering, a ≥90° line-referenced pitch range (flag-out) and depower; flyer air data (pitot + AoA vane + IMU) and a radio link; a pack reel with fairlead shock spring; launch only on straight glides; dock only while still moving (or land beside); hard safety elements (weak link, line cutter) rather than abort logic.
pack: ICM-42688-class IMU + MAX-M10S GNSS (10 Hz) + BMP390; detector as lib/detect.mjs (speed 2.8 m/s, descent, vibration, from-rest, post-lift lockout 30 m) + session arming + OSM aerialway geofence
MN3508-class (or 6S, Ø32 mm drum) reel, FOC current loop ≥1000 rad/s, 500 Hz velocity loop with tension feed-forward; ≥250 W burst ESC
HX711 + 5 kg cell on the fairlead pulley, two AS5600 on a gimballed exit arm, 150 N/m series shock spring, level-wind
weak link ≈15–20 N at the pack (ASSUMED), line cutter, dock latch sensor
flyer: roll actuator (steering), bridle pitch actuator −80…+10° (flag-out), spoilers/depower
pitot (SDP3x class) + AoA vane + IMU; 100 Hz ELRS-class link
AoA loop (target from force demand, ≥2.5° below stall), spoiler loop on window elevation (target 65°), roll loop to the mean-course window centre
recommendedArchitecture.modes: STOWED → (ride detected ∧ straight glide ∧ va ≥1.3 V_stall) LAUNCH (≤2 m/s pay-out to 6 m) → FLY (admittance reel law, surplus paid out to 12–15 m) → RETRIEVE on stop gesture / decel / geofence / low lift → DOCK while moving or LAND beside → STOWED; ABORT on fall = weak link + flag-out.

failureModes.mode: flyer whipped/stalled at short line during carving, hits snow
failureModes.mitigation: launch on straight glide only, fast but ≤2 m/s pay-out to ≥6 m, abort-to-dock on first stall

failureModes.mode: power-zone trap (AoA 40–90°) behind the skier, dragged on snow, tension >100 N
failureModes.mitigation: flag-out pitch range, weak link, payout limit at Lmax

failureModes.mode: lateral divergence to window edge, AoA collapse

failureModes.mitigation: spoiler elevation loop, force target > weight

failureModes.mode: tether-only wind estimate diverges (unobservable axis + calibration)
failureModes.mitigation: flyer air data; never gate safety on tether-only wind

failureModes.mode: KE >14.9 J from skier speed + swings
failureModes.mitigation: ≤40–60 g flyer or soft/frangible structure; rider-frame argument not available >1.5 m

failureModes.mode: fast dock (≥4 m/s) after a stop in calm
failureModes.mitigation: dock while moving; land beside; compliant funnel

failureModes.mode: fall: flyer dragged onto the fallen skier, 50 N on the line
false launch on unload ramp / in a bus
line passes within ≈0.01–0.08 m of the helmet centre (headClear fail)
failureModes.mitigation: exit point above/behind helmet on a short mast, or tail-mounted exit; needs geometry study

limitations: Point-mass flyer; no rotational dynamics, no wake of the skier, crude stall/flat-plate blend; roll disturbance is an ASSUMED stochastic process.

Controllers are first-iteration designs by one scientist in one session; poor closed-loop numbers are an upper bound on difficulty only where backed by the physics findings above; better controllers may do better (the oracle variants bound how much estimation alone explains).
Activity traces for detection are synthetic; no measured ski IMU data used.
Snow contact is Coulomb friction μ=0.3 (ASSUMED); avalanche of snow contacts may be pessimistic or optimistic.
No camera-based estimation simulated (argued: a flyer camera bearing inherits the 3° flyer attitude error ⇒ no better than the exit angle at 12–15 m).
